note: CIBC Caribbean's St Lucia schedule of charges for cards (effective December 2019, last updated September 2026), read in full: the personal cards in Eastern Caribbean dollars and US dollars are written, each with its annual fee for the primary card (none where the schedule gives 0.00; the British Airways Visa Platinum's waived for its first year), its yearly purchase rate, its cash advance rate and 3.50% cash advance fee, its 1.01% foreign transaction fee on the Eastern Caribbean dollar cards, its late payment, over limit and returned cheque fees, and its late payment rate as the penalty rate. The two US dollar cards carry their own fees; their only foreign transaction fee in the schedule is on Barbados dollar transactions, which isn't written. The UWI cards are for the University of the West Indies' students, faculty and alumni, a condition the game doesn't check; the UWI rewards card's waiver for faculty isn't written. The commercial and business cards aren't written; nor are the replacement card, statement, rush card, emergency payment and auto-payment charges, which a holder meets only by asking or by an auto-payment. The schedule states no minimum payment or grace period for the personal cards. Republic Bank's St Lucia Republic Mastercard page, its rates and fees table (in effect as of September 1, 2021), read in full: the Republic Bank Mastercard, Mastercard Gold and AAdvantage Mastercard, all fees in Eastern Caribbean dollars, each with its annual membership fee for the primary card, 22% a year on purchases and balance transfers (the bank says the rate is set on approval and could be 22%, the only figure it gives), a minimum payment of 2.77% of the principal balance plus the period's interest (the 'any other fees' it also adds aren't modelled), a cash advance fee of 3.2% with a floor, the late payment, returned cheque and over limit charges, and an interest-free period of at least 50 days on purchases when the statement is paid in full (written as 50). The replacement card and statement charges aren't written. The page states no foreign transaction fee or penalty rate. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) looked for more banks and added none: the RBC Caribbean credit card pages, rendered, list no personal card for the Eastern Caribbean, only business cards; the Bank of Saint Lucia's card pages give no figures ('low annual fee', 'competitive interest rates') and 1st National Bank's site didn't answer.
